summary: Gone steel fire tower about five miles south of Paoli in Orange County, known also as the Valeene tower. Built around 1933-34; taken down; site today undescribed.

facts.design: Steel fire tower, 100 feet (1932 plan, 1933 description)
facts.status_note: Not standing; the 2025 chapter report says it was taken down

events.note: Indianapolis News item (August 20, 1932): a new steel tower of 80 to 100 feet was to be built at the Marengo and English highways junction; a state forestry representative had obtained the site.
Planned watch of three months in spring and three in fall. A plan, not confirmed.
Forest Worker (January 1933) describes a 100-foot tower about 5 miles south of Paoli as existing. The Herald gives 1934 for the build year.
Dubois County Herald: photographed shortly after it was built in 1934. Conflicts with the January 1933 description.
Nearby FIRE survey-marker datasheet says the tower still existed in 1965.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources use Paoli, Valeene and Orange for one site. The Herald and the 2025 chapter report place the tower on the Valeene road south of Paoli, which fits the Indiana Fire Towers description. The match to the record's coordinates is not checked.

notes_for_editor: Build year conflict is not resolved: the January 1933 Forest Worker description and the 1932 plan point to 1932-33, while the Herald says it was built in 1934. The Herald's Valeene tower is treated as the FFLA Paoli (Orange) tower by name and place, but the record's coordinates (38.49046, -86.43784) were not checked against the Valeene road description. The Herald is a reprint of a heritage project. The 2025 chapter report's source for 'no longer standing' is a local informant's account. No source describes the site today or whether it is public. Staffing item is from the 1932 plan only; the Herald names watchers without dates.
